Page 1/8 
Name: Gowtham Gopalakrishnan Iyer 
GIT URL of code: colab/ML_Coding_Assignment_U1A1_LR_GI.ipynb at main · GowthamGIyer/colab 
(github.com) 
 
Machine Learning (BMI/GEO/WNA) 
Code Assignment U1A1  
Linear Regression 
This is NOT a group Assignment. 
 
10 marks 
Please complete seeing the videos for Week 1-2 before attempting this 
assignment.  
 
Use real estate valuation regression dataset : 
https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/477/real+estate+valuation+data+set  from 
the UCI repository, and use google colab to code. 
 
First, download the csv file, and open it in your computer and analyze the data. 
Try to understand what the data is about. Read through the data description 
given 
in 
the 
UCI 
website 
as 
well. 
 
Section A 
Answer the following questions [1 mark if you answer all the below questions]: 
 
1. How many samples are there? 
Response: There are 414 samples. 
 
2. How many input variables are there? 
Response: There are 6 input variables. 
 
3. Which column is the output variable (target outcome)? 
Response: The output variable is “Y house price of unit area”, column 
“H” in the dataset.

Page 2/8 
4. What does each of the input columns mean? 
Response: Meaning of input columns in the dataset is described in 
below table: 
Input Column 
Type 
Description 
X1 transaction date 
Continuous Transaction date. The digits before the decimal 
represent the year of transaction. The month is 
represented by the digits immediately after the 
decimal in a scale of 0 to 11 (Jan to Dec). 
X2 house age 
Continuous Age of the house (in years). 
X3 distance to the 
nearest MRT station 
Continuous Distance to the nearest MRT station (in meters). 
X4 number of 
convenience stores 
Integer 
Number of convenience stores within walkable 
distance. 
X5 latitude 
Continuous Latitude coordinate (in degrees). 
X6 longitude 
Continuous Longitude coordinate (in degrees). 
 
Section B 
For each of the questions below, you need to put in the screenshot of the code 
and its output. You could use the sample google colab file that is provided with 
this assignment. 
1. Understanding the dataset [4 marks] 
There are many input variables in this dataset. Use only X1 to X4 as input 
variables, and y as the output variable. 
Using the scatter plots between each of the input features (X1-X4) and the 
output (Y), which input variable, do you think, is better in predicting the output 
/ target variable? 
 
Scatter plots:

Page 3/8 
 
 
 
 
 
Response: The X3 input variable (Distance to nearest MRT station) is better in 
predicting the output variable (House Price per unit area) since the scatter plot 
between this input variable and the output variable shows a clear Negative 
Correlation (price reduces with increasing distance). The prediction line also 
supports this. 
Number of convenience stores comes next in terms of prediction efficiency. 
In case of other inputs there is no clear correlation. For example, in case of 
“Transaction Date” input, all output values are mapped to only a few input 
values. Since there are multiple output values per input value, predictability 
reduces.

Page 4/8 
Screenshot of code snippet to generate feature-wise scatter plots against the 
output variable:

Page 5/8 
 
 
2. Write code to find out how many samples are there in total in this dataset? [1 
mark] 
 
Screenshot of code snippet, and its output, to find total number of samples in 
the dataset:

Page 6/8 
3. What is the train test split ratio that you have chosen? [1 Mark] 
 
Screenshot of code snippet for train-test split ratio: 
 
Response: I have chosen train set of ratio 2/3 and test set of ratio 1/3 (this is 
also advised in the “Real Estate Valuation” - dataset information section). 
 
 
4. Evaluate the linear regression model by computing the MAE, MSE and Mean 
Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) . 
(for MAPE - pls refer to the sample here - https://scikit-
learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.mean_absolute_percent
age_error.html)  
[3 marks]

Page 7/8 
Screenshot of code snippet for evaluating the model using MAE, MSE and 
MAPE and its corresponding output: 
 
 
 
5. What are the 3 new things that you learned after you completed this 
assignment? 
 
Response: Three new things that I learnt after completing this assignment: 
• Using packages related to Machine Learning in Python (Scikit). 
• Practical usage of Linear Regression model on a real-world dataset. 
• Meaning, definition and computing (using Python) of Mean Absolute 
Percentage Error.

Page 8/8 
Grading Scheme (Total 10 Marks) 
Time - 4 hours max. 
Submission on Teams by 11.30 PM, 20 Feb 2024. 
Late submissions are NOT allowed. 
 
Plagiarism Policy 
You are NOT allowed to discuss. You cannot copy paste text/image from the internet or 
other sources. All assignments are put through TurnitIn, and any similarity score of more 
than 40% will be flagged as plagiarism. The penalties are as follows. 
● 1st instance of plagiarism - 0 marks for this assignment 
● 2nd instance of plagiarism - GRADE DOWN for the entire course 
● 3rd instance of plagiarism - FAIL in the course 
 
By submitting this assignment, you agree to the above policies on grading, submission and 
plagiarism.
